newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank sector start new talks on sick pay.
newsitem.headline: German bank sector start new talks on sick pay.

text.p: New talks between Germany's banking employers and the main trade unions in the sector over threatened cuts to sick pay started on Monday after two previous sets of discussions broke down.
At issue is a 20 percent cut in German sick pay entitlements made possible by a new law introduced late last year and which German banks had initially implemented.
However, following mass worker protests the banks later backed down, saying they would seek to gain a definitive agreement on the issue with negotiators from the two trade unions in the sector.

Gerhard Renner, chief negotiator for the DAG white-collar workers trade union, indicated on Saturday that the union was prepared to give some ground on future wage increases in return for retaining full sick pay and measures on job protection.
If no agreement is reached in these or further talks on sick pay, the whole issue is likely to be handled within the 1997 banking sector wage round due to start later this year.
